input: Find bribery and market-manipulation enforcement actions involving Glencore since 2018

entity.hq_country: Switzerland (headquarters in Baar; registered office in Saint Helier, Jersey)
entity.group: Glencore group (Glencore plc and its subsidiaries, including Glencore International AG, Glencore Ltd., Glencore Energy UK Ltd and Chemoil Corporation)

events.amount: USD 700,706,965 gross (USD 428,521,173 fine + USD 272,185,792 forfeiture/disgorgement), before credits for payments to other authorities; as_of 2022-05-24
events.summary: Glencore International AG pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to violate the US Foreign Corrupt Practices Act and agreed to an independent compliance monitor for three years.

events.jurisdiction: United States (DOJ; federal court in Connecticut)
events.status: convicted (guilty plea; sentenced by a Connecticut federal judge, reported 2022-09-23)
events.summary: Glencore Ltd. pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to manipulate fuel-oil prices, and a Connecticut federal judge later imposed the plea-agreement terms of about USD 485 million, including a three-year monitor.

events.type: Market manipulation and corruption (civil, Commodity Exchange Act)
events.parties: Glencore International A.G., Glencore Ltd., Chemoil Corporation
events.amount: USD 1,186,345,850 total (USD 865,630,784 civil penalty + USD 320,715,066 disgorgement), partly offset against DOJ payments; as_of 2022-05-24
events.summary: The CFTC found that from 2007 to at least 2018 Glencore manipulated or tried to manipulate four US S&P Global Platts fuel-oil benchmarks and related derivatives, paid bribes to state-owned-company staff in Brazil, Cameroon, Nigeria and Venezuela, and misused confidential information from employees of a Mexican state-owned company.

Glencore reached a resolution with Brazil's MPF over bribery allegations involving Petrobras, reportedly about USD 29.6 million in compensation to Petrobras and about USD 10 million in civil penalties.

events.amount: GBP 280,965,092.95 in penalty, confiscation and costs; as_of 2022-11-03
events.summary: Charged on 24 May 2022 with seven bribery counts over more than USD 25 million in bribes by agents and employees to get preferential access to oil in Nigeria, Cameroon, Ivory Coast, Equatorial Guinea and South Sudan, the company pleaded guilty to all counts and received the UK's largest-ever corporate criminal penalty.

events.type: Corruption (civil settlement with a foreign state)
events.summary: Glencore agreed to pay the DRC USD 180 million to settle all present and future claims from alleged corruption in 2007–2018; the US DOJ had said Glencore paid USD 27.5 million to third parties intending part of it to bribe Congolese officials.

events.type: Bribery (corporate failure to prevent bribery of foreign public officials)
events.status: convicted (summary penalty order, not contested; other DRC facts from 2007–2017 partly abandoned)
events.amount: CHF 2 million fine + USD 150 million compensation claim; as_of 2024-08-05
events.summary: The Swiss OAG held Glencore International AG criminally liable for failing to take reasonable organisational measures to prevent a business partner from bribing DRC officials in 2011, when the partner bought minority stakes in two Congolese mining companies.

events.parties: Glencore International AG (investigation of unnamed co-defendants continues)
events.summary: The Dutch Public Prosecution Service dropped its case against Glencore International AG because Switzerland had concluded the investigation with a summary penalty order, and the two countries agreed a Swiss conclusion was preferable for a Swiss company.

events.type: Bribery (conspiracy to make corrupt payments; falsifying documents)
events.status: charged (not-guilty pleas from Hopkirk, Labiaga, Wakefield and Perez on 2025-11-10 and from Beard and Gibson in September 2026; trial listed for 2027-10-04)
events.parties: Former Glencore employees Alex Beard (former head of oil), Andrew Gibson, Paul Hopkirk, Ramon Labiaga, Martin Wakefield, David Perez
events.summary: The SFO charged six former Glencore employees with conspiring to make corrupt payments linked to oil contracts in Nigeria, Cameroon and Ivory Coast from 2007 to 2014; Gibson, Wakefield and Perez also face charges of falsifying documents over service fees to a Nigerian oil consultancy.

output.assessment: Risk is high on history but the corporate matters are largely closed. Glencore entities pleaded guilty or were found liable for foreign bribery in the US, UK and Switzerland and for oil-benchmark manipulation in the US, paying over USD 1.5 billion in coordinated 2022 resolutions plus USD 180 million to the DRC and CHF 2 million plus USD 150 million in Switzerland. Still open: the UK SFO trial of six former employees, including former head of oil Alex Beard, listed for 4 October 2027 (Spotlight on Corruption reported in January 2026 that the lead SFO prosecutors were leaving); the Dutch investigation of unnamed co-defendants; and confirmation that the US probation and three-year monitorships have ended, which I could not verify.
